extra_misconceptions.fact: Shipping fees, installation charges, mandatory accessories, and energy operating costs often make a low sticker price more expensive.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The store offering the lowest advertised sticker price always provides the cheapest total purchase cost for a major item.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Retail prices reflect brand marketing and store markup, so buyers must check independent reliability ratings and warranty terms.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A higher retail price tag guarantees superior build quality, longer product lifespan, and lower maintenance costs over time.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Extended warranties often duplicate the manufacturer's standard coverage and contain strict exclusions that rarely justify their cost.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Extended store warranties are always worth purchasing because they cover every possible repair or accidental damage for free.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A reliable family savings plan treats the monthly savings target as a fixed budget transfer scheduled before discretionary spending.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saving for a major family purchase only requires setting aside whatever leftover cash remains at the end of each month.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a family's emergency cash reserve when a major appliance purchase is funded without a dedicated savings plan?
Which total-cost metrics beyond the sticker price must you record when comparing three competing retailers for the same item?
Under what condition does waiting for a seasonal clearance sale actually end up costing your family more money overall?
Why is it dangerous to evaluate product quality solely by brand reputation or the highest retail price tag in the store?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An effective budget requires weekly comparison against actual tracked receipts so spending categories can be adjusted in real time.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A personal budget is a one-time forecast written at the start of the quarter and left untouched until the 13 weeks end.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unrecorded micro-purchases compound over 91 days and frequently account for the largest gap between planned and actual savings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Small daily cash purchases like snacks or drinks are too minor to affect a 13-week savings goal and do not need logging.

extra_misconceptions.fact: One-time gifts or irregular job payouts are non-recurring income and should be routed to savings rather than ongoing fixed expenses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An unexpected cash windfall during Week 4 permanently increases the safe weekly spending limit for the remaining nine weeks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Zero-based budgeting assigns every dollar a job, which includes allocating a dedicated portion directly into a savings reserve.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Balancing a budget means spending every dollar of projected income so that the final net balance equals exactly zero.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your 13-week budget accuracy when small cash purchases under five dollars are omitted from your daily ledger?
Which ledger figure confirms whether your actual 13-week cash flow resulted in a net surplus or a budget deficit?
Under what condition does cutting an expense category fail to balance a budget where projected outflows exceed income?
Where should a Scout record irregular cash gifts or chore bonuses so they do not distort regular weekly spending limits?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unplanned discount purchases still reduce your cash balance and represent spending rather than genuine financial savings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buying an item marked fifty percent off saves you money even if you had no prior need or budgeted plan to buy that product.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Retailers sometimes price bulk packages at a higher unit cost, so comparing the shelf tag's price per ounce is essential.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Larger family-size packages in a supermarket always carry a lower cost per ounce than standard or smaller package sizes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lifetime warranties typically cover only the expected useful market life of the product as defined by the manufacturer's fine print.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A product labeled with a lifetime guarantee will be repaired or replaced for the entire lifespan of the original buyer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hedonic adaptation causes the initial novelty of new possessions to fade quickly, often leading to buyer's remorse within months.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Emotional satisfaction from buying a trendy non-essential item remains just as strong ninety days after the purchase date.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your impulse-buying resistance when you shop at a grocery store on an empty stomach without a written list?
Which psychological trigger causes the excitement of a brand-new purchase to fade noticeably within three months of ownership?
Under what condition does carrying a large amount of physical cash or a tap-to-pay card alter your willingness to overspend?
Why is it dangerous to rely on front-of-box marketing claims instead of calculating the unit price per ounce on the shelf tag?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Saving preserves liquid principal for short-term needs at low yields, while investing accepts market risk for long-term growth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saving and investing are identical financial strategies that both guarantee your principal balance will never lose value.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Simple interest pays only on the original principal, whereas compound interest calculates new earnings on principal plus prior interest.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Simple interest and compound interest produce the exact same total account balance as long as the stated annual rate matches.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Risk and potential return are directly linked in financial markets, and any promise of high guaranteed returns is a warning sign.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High-return investments with zero risk of principal loss are regularly available to careful investors who research the market.

extra_misconceptions.fact: True diversification spreads capital across uncorrelated asset classes and industries so a single sector downturn does not sink all funds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Diversification means buying shares in five different technology companies that all make smartphone hardware and software.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the purchasing power of cash held in a zero-interest jar when annual inflation exceeds three percent?
Which mathematical mechanism makes compound interest grow exponentially faster than simple interest over a multi-decade horizon?
Under what condition does an investor choose a low-yield savings account over a higher-return equity investment?
Why is it dangerous to concentrate your entire long-term investment portfolio inside a single company or industry sector?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Common stock represents partial equity ownership with no guaranteed price or dividend, unlike a bond that represents a debt loan.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Purchasing a share of common stock makes you a creditor of the corporation and guarantees a fixed quarterly dividend payment.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Certificates of deposit lock in funds for a fixed term and charge early withdrawal penalties if redeemed before maturity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A certificate of deposit allows penalty-free cash withdrawals at any time just like a standard bank savings or checking account.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mutual funds hold market securities that fluctuate in value and carry zero FDIC protection against investment principal losses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mutual funds are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation against market declines up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars.

extra_misconceptions.fact: U.S. savings bonds are non-marketable government debt instruments that cannot be redeemed during the first twelve months of ownership.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: U.S. savings bonds can be traded on public stock exchanges and cashed out three weeks after purchase without restriction.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the accrued interest on a bank certificate of deposit if you withdraw your principal before the maturity date?
Which ownership right distinguishes a common stockholder from a bondholder who lends money to the federal government?
Under what condition does a mutual fund provide lower single-company risk than purchasing individual shares of common stock?
What measurement confirms the annual administrative cost deducted from your assets inside an actively managed mutual fund?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A landlord's policy insures only the physical building structure, requiring tenants to carry renter's insurance for personal belongings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A landlord's property insurance policy automatically covers a renter's personal clothing, electronics, and furniture during a fire.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Term life provides pure death-benefit coverage for a set period with no cash value, whereas whole life includes a savings component.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Term life insurance builds a guaranteed tax-deferred cash value account that the policyholder can borrow against at any age.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Low deductibles trigger significantly higher monthly premiums that often cost more over time than maintaining an emergency deductible fund.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Choosing the lowest possible insurance deductible always saves a policyholder the most money over several claim-free years.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A deductible is the annual amount you pay before insurance shares costs, while a copayment is a flat fee paid per medical service.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Health insurance copayments and annual deductibles are identical fees that stop applying after your first doctor visit each year.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your monthly insurance premium when you raise the policy deductible from two hundred fifty to one thousand dollars?
Which policy feature distinguishes permanent whole life insurance from a pure twenty-year term life insurance contract?
Under what condition does a landlord's building insurance policy refuse to pay for a tenant's stolen laptop and damaged furniture?
Why is it dangerous to drive an automobile carrying only collision coverage while omitting bodily injury and property liability?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A debit card withdraws your own cash immediately from checking and does not build credit, while a credit card borrows issuer funds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A debit card and a credit card both create a short-term bank loan that builds your credit score when paid at the end of the month.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paying only the minimum avoids late fees but leaves the unpaid balance accruing high compound interest that can take years to clear.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Paying the minimum required monthly payment on a credit card statement prevents interest from accruing on the remaining balance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Annual Percentage Rate includes upfront loan origination fees and closing costs alongside the base interest rate to show true cost.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A loan's stated nominal interest rate and its Annual Percentage Rate are always identical numbers on a consumer loan contract.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A charge card requires the entire statement balance to be paid in full every billing cycle and does not permit revolving monthly debt.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A traditional charge card lets you revolve an unpaid balance from month to month just like a standard revolving credit card.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the total repayment cost and payoff timeline of a credit card balance when you pay only the monthly minimum?
Which cost components are captured by the Annual Percentage Rate that are hidden when looking only at the nominal interest rate?
Under what condition does using a credit card cost the borrower zero dollars in interest charges while building credit history?
Where should you look on a loan disclosure statement to verify the true total dollar amount you will pay over the loan's life?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Prioritizing tasks by true importance and deadline impact ensures critical responsibilities are completed before trivial quick chores.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An effective weekly to-do list ranks tasks strictly by which assignment can be finished the fastest for a quick sense of progress.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over-packed schedules collapse at the first delay, so realistic calendars include buffer blocks for travel, rest, and unexpected tasks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A seven-day schedule only works if every single hour is booked solid with zero unscheduled buffer time between daily activities.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Keeping a daily log of actual time spent alongside the planned schedule is required to spot time-wasters and improve future estimates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Writing a weekly calendar guarantees good time management even if you never track how your actual hours were spent each day.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rapidly switching attention between tasks increases errors and mental fatigue, making focused single-task blocks far more efficient.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Multitasking between homework, text messages, and chores finishes all three tasks faster than completing them one at a time.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to high-priority long-term goals when a Scout schedules urgent but low-importance distractions first each afternoon?
Which entries must be blocked onto your seven-day calendar first before slotting in flexible personal projects or leisure time?
What measurement in your daily time diary reveals where unplanned interruptions or procrastination derailed your written schedule?
Why is it dangerous to pack a seven-day calendar wall-to-wall with zero buffer blocks between homework, chores, and troop meetings?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 9 is strictly a written planning exercise on paper and does not require executing the physical project.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Requirement 9 requires executing the planned event in real life with your patrol before the counselor signs off.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Resources include human skills, volunteer labor, facilities, permits, and borrowed equipment alongside purchased items.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A project resource list only includes physical tools and purchased supplies that have a direct dollar price tag.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An effective timeline orders tasks sequentially from start to finish with target dates and task dependencies.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A project timeline is complete as soon as every required task is written down in an unnumbered checklist.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Borrowed and donated items must still be documented in the resource list with their specific roles in reaching the goal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Donated supplies and borrowed troop gear can be left out of the project plan because they cost zero dollars.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your project completion date when two dependent timeline tasks are scheduled to start on the same day?
What separates a measurable project goal in step 9a from the detailed activity description required in step 9c?
Which budget line items change when a donated material or volunteer skill from your resource list becomes unavailable?
Under what condition does a written project budget require a contingency reserve before you finalize the timeline?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Total career preparation costs also include room and board, books, tools, licensing exams, and transportation expenses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Published college or trade school tuition represents the entire out-of-pocket cost of earning a career credential.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts may explore skilled trades, military service, technical certifications, or university degree career paths.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career discussed for Requirement 10 must require a four-year university bachelor degree after high school.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Grants and scholarships are gift aid, whereas student loans must be repaid with interest according to contract terms.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Student loans, grants, and scholarships all work the same way because none of them require repayment after graduation.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts can build relevant experience early through internships, part-time jobs, volunteering, and related merit badges.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Relevant career experience can only be gained after completing all formal college degrees or trade certifications.

extra_socratic_questions: Which entry-level credentials or apprenticeships can you complete during high school to test your chosen career field?
What separates published college tuition rates from the total cost of attendance you must finance each academic year?
What happens to your net educational loan balance when unsubsidized interest accrues during four years of training?
Under what condition does combining scholarships, part-time work, and in-state tuition close a career funding gap?
